question: What is the primary fluid transported within the lymphatic vessels called?
explanation: Fluid that enters the lymphatic vessels from the interstitial spaces is specifically referred to as lymph. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why does the body require a functional lymphatic system alongside the cardiovascular system?

options.A: To generate the primary red blood cells required for tissue respiration
options.B: To return filtered interstitial fluid and proteins back to the blood circulation
options.C: To digest complex dietary fats within the large intestine
options.D: To pump oxygenated blood directly to deep skeletal muscle tissues

explanation: The lymphatic system acts as a drainage system to recover fluid and proteins that continuously leak out of blood capillaries. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which structural feature prevents lymph from flowing backward inside collecting vessels?
explanation: Lymphatic vessels contain numerous internal valves that ensure fluid moves in only one direction toward the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: A patient on prolonged bed rest experiences dependent lower extremity edema partly due to sluggish lymphatic return. What is the primary physiological reason lymph moves slowly in this patient?

options.B: Immediate collapse of the primary lymph capillaries
options.C: Complete destruction of all thoracic valves
options.D: Failure of the left ventricle to generate pressure

explanation: Lymph propulsion relies heavily on the milking action of active skeletal muscles surrounding the vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: Through which type of vessel does lymph enter a lymph node?
explanation: Afferent lymphatic vessels carry unfiltered lymph directly into the lymph node for processing. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary physiological consequence when regional lymph nodes become tender and swollen during an infection?

options.A: Sudden blockage of all efferent vessels causing total fluid rupture
options.B: Direct invasion of red blood cells into the lymphatic cortex
options.C: Active proliferation and immune response of lymphocytes within the node
options.D: Permanent cessation of local interstitial fluid filtration

explanation: Swelling occurs because white blood cells rapidly multiply inside the node to fight off the trapped pathogens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which specific anatomical structure drains lymph from the lower extremities and the entire left side of the body?
explanation: The thoracic duct collects lymph from both lower limbs, the abdomen, and the entire left upper quadrant of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Where do the main lymphatic ducts ultimately empty their fluid contents into the cardiovascular system?
explanation: Terminal lymphatic ducts empty directly into the venous blood near the junction of the internal jugular and subclavian veins. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which accessory lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and recycling aged red blood cells?
explanation: The spleen acts as a blood filter that removes defective red blood cells and stores platelets. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the thymus gland during early development?

options.A: Filtration of interstitial lymph from the lower extremities
options.B: Absorption of dietary fats from the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Production of clotting factors and blood plasma proteins

explanation: The thymus provides the hormonal and physical microenvironment necessary for T-cell maturation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the clinical term for localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic drainage pathway?
explanation: Lymphedema describes the swelling that develops when lymphatic fluid accumulates in the interstitial spaces due to vessel obstruction or damage. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h6)

question: A patient has undergone a radical mastectomy with complete right axillary lymph node removal. Which nursing action is essential to prevent secondary complications in the right arm?

options.A: Encouraging heavy weightlifting exercises to force open new vessels
options.B: Applying ice packs continuously to constrict local lymphatic channels
options.C: Elevating the left arm above the heart level during rest periods
options.D: Avoiding blood pressure measurements and venipunctures on the right arm

explanation: Protecting the compromised limb from trauma and skin punctures prevents bacteria from entering, which easily triggers severe cellulitis in lymphedematous tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h6)
